name: SR Linux/SROS Streaming Telemetry Lab
what_it_is: A Containerlab-based lab that deploys a small Clos/DCI fabric with Nokia SR Linux leaves and spines and Nokia SR OS (SR-SIM) DC gateways, wired to a complete streaming telemetry stack (gnmic, Prometheus, Grafana). It demonstrates gNMI dial-in telemetry collection, EVPN/eBGP underlay/overlay, and interactive traffic-driven weathermap dashboards.
components: Nokia SR Linux (IXR-D2L leaves, IXR-D3L spines) — containerized NOS
Nokia SR OS via SR-SIM (SR-1 DC gateways) — requires active SR-SIM license
gnmic 0.41.0 — gNMI collector and subscription manager
network-multitool — six Linux client nodes with iperf3 servers
traffic.sh — script to start/stop iperf3 traffic between client pairs
protocols: gNMI (dial-in, sample / on-change / target-defined subscription modes)
eBGP (underlay routing between leaves, spines, and DC gateways)
iBGP (overlay EVPN service between leaves and DC gateways)
measurement: SR Linux: 100% YANG coverage of state and config data via gNMI
SR OS (SR-SIM): sample, target-defined, and on-change telemetry via dial-in or dial-out
Link rate and utilization — visualized in Grafana weathermap (flow-panel plugin)
iperf3 throughput — generated by traffic.sh between client pairs or all nodes
Prometheus scrape of gnmic-exported metrics at http://localhost:9090
configuration: Topology defined in st.clab.yml (single file, Containerlab format)
Management subnet: 172.80.80.0/24; static IPs for all nodes
Grafana preconfigured with anonymous access and flow-panel plugin enabled
Deploy: clab deploy; Destroy: clab destroy
modes: on-change subscription — gNMI event-driven updates on state change
sample subscription — gNMI periodic polling at fixed intervals
target-defined subscription — NOS chooses the appropriate mode per path
dial-in telemetry — collector initiates gNMI session to the node
dial-out telemetry — node initiates gNMI session to the collector (SR OS)
constraints: Nokia SR OS DC gateway nodes (dcgw1, dcgw2) require an active SR-SIM license downloaded from Nokia Support Portal — lab cannot run SR OS nodes without it
Containerlab must be installed on the host; the topology is Containerlab-native and has no docker-compose equivalent
Grafana flow-panel (weathermap) plugin must be present in the Grafana image; the lab pins grafana/grafana:11.2.0 which bundles it
Six client nodes use network-multitool image with iperf3 — traffic generation depends on iperf3 availability inside those containers
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml — lab is Containerlab-native only
No fault injection or link failure scenarios defined in the lab files
No CI/automated test suite visible in the repository
No NETCONF or RESTCONF interfaces exposed or documented
